newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus equities lose 1.26 percent in week.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus equities lose 1.26 percent in week.

text.p: Cyprus equities closed 1.26 percent lower during the week spurred by lack of enthusiasm and a wave of selling that hit the bourse, analysts said.
The general index of the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) was 76.75 points on Friday, after closing at 77.73 pounds on May 9.
In a weekly commentary CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation said the market lacked enthusiasm.
"There is still no concrete evidence that the economy and specifically tourism will really perform better than expected," CISCO said.

Tourism, which contributes 22 percent to the gross national product of the island, was down by around three percent last year, according to the most-recent official estimates. Tourism officials expect the number of tourists who visited in 1996 -- 1.9 million -- will be matched this year.
CISCO also said the stock market was governed by a "narrow time horizon".
"Some investors are getting out of the market with small gains and are re-entering when they believe there is room for small gains," CISCO said.
Declines were registered in six of the sub indices with the exception of insurance companies, which recorded gains of 1.10 percent.

The Bank of Cyprus announced a 2.6 percent rise in its Q1 1997 earnings to 7.9 million pounds in operating profits from 7.7 million registered in the corresponding period for 1996. The group announced it expects 1997 results of the group are expected to show about the same growth as that of the first quarter.
Its middle market trading price was 304.5 cents on Friday, down 6.5 cents from last week.
Trading in Bank of Cyprus shares accounted for 32 percent of total trade on Friday, followed by partly paid shares of Hellenic Bank, with 11 percent of overall trade.
Shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 304.5 cents, up 1.5 cents on last week's middle market trading price.
Fully paid shares of the Hellenic Bank were trading at 280.5 cents, three cents up on last week, while fully paid shares of the Universal Savings Bank closed at 185.5, down 2.5 cents.

Insurance company Universal Life shares were trading at 458 cents on Friday, gaining 24.5 cents. Interamerican shares were trading for 97.5 cents from 99 last week. Associate company Philiki fully paid closed at 259, dropping two cents.
Shares in the Cyprus Tourist Development Company owners of the Cyprus Hilton, were trading for 775 cents on Friday from 761 cents last week.
